sentences.text:
Both appeals arise out of judgment and award dated 04th August, 2018 passed in MVC No.1948 of 2015 by the X Additional District Judge and Member of Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Belagavi (for short hereinafter referred to as the "Tribunal").

entities.text:
Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Belagavi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, parties in these appeals are referred to with their rank and status before the Tribunal.

3. Relevant facts leading to filing of these appeals are that, the claimant preferred Claim Petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident.

In the claim petition it is stated that on 10th July, 2015 at about 1.00 pm,
one Omkar Mallappa Ajagolkar being the rider of motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-22/EJ-4014 while proceeding on Vijayanagar Pipeline Road from Ganeshpur-Belegavi Main Road to Hindalga-Belagavi Main Road, rode the motorcycle in a high speed, rash and negligent manner and when he reached near Vijayanagar Kannada Marathi School, he dashed against another motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-22/W-2009 NC: 2024:KHC-D:7834-DB which was coming from opposite direction and the impact of the accident is that the claimant, who was a pillion rider on the motorcycle bearing Registration No.KA-22/EJ-4014, suffered grievous injuries.

Immediately,
he was taken to BIMS Hospital, Belagavi for treatment and after receiving first aid therein, he was shifted to Vijaya Hospital, Belagavi for better treatment.
Further, it is stated as to the age and occupation of the petitioner and also as to the permanent physical disability suffered on account of accident.
On all the grounds sought for compensation.
4. In response to service of notice, respondents 1 and 2 entered appearance through their Advocate and filed statement of objections.

The respondent No.1 has denied the entire averments made in the petition as false and she has taken up further contention that the rider of the motorcycle No.KA-22/W-2009 was riding the motorcycle in drunken condition and in a high speed, rash and negligent manner and abruptly came on the right side of the road and dashed against the motorcycle of respondent No.1 and accordingly, the claimant is not entitled for any compensation.
On all these grounds, sought for dismissal of claim petition.
Respondent No.2-Insurance Company also denied the entire averments made in the claim petition as false.

Further, it is stated that the motorcycle bearing Registration No.KA-22/EJ-4014 owned by respondent No.1 was insured with respondent No.2-Insurance Company from 21st July,
2015 to 20th July, 2016 and was not insured with the respondent No.2- Insurance Company as on the date of accident, i.e. 10th July, 2015, and as such, the respondent No.2 is not liable to pay any Smt.Rajashree Mallappa Rajgolkar vs Sri.Sagar Maruti Bokade on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168445545/
3 compensation to the claimant.

entities.text: Rajashree Mallappa Rajgolkar vs Sri.Sagar Maruti Bokade
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On all these grounds sought for dismissal of claim petition.
6. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Tribunal has framed appropriate issues.
To prove the case of the petitioner, two witnesses were examined as PWs.1 and 2 and seventeen documents were marked as Exhibits P1 to P17.
On closure of the petitioner's side evidence, one Arati W/o Amarendra Kanago, was examined as RW1 and two documents were marked as Exhibits R1 and R2.

Having heard the arguments on both sides, the Tribunal allowed the claim petition in part and awarded compensation of Rs.24,00,960/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realisation and directed the respondent NC: 2024:KHC-D:7834-DB No.1-onwer of the vehicle, to pay the award amount.

Against the said Judgment and Award dated 04th August, 2018, the owner of the motorcycle-Smt. Rajashree, preferred Civil Review Petition No.8 of 2018 under Section 114 read with Order XLVII Rule 1 and Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure before the X Additional District and Sessions Judge, Belagavi seeking review of the judgment and award.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The X Additional District and Sessions Judge, by order dated 05th April, 2019,
dismissed the Review Petition.

Being aggrieved by the Judgment and Award dated 04th August,
2018 passed in MVC No.1948 of 2015, has preferred MFA No.102573 of 2019 seeking setting aside of the Judgment and Award, by allowing the appeal.
7. Petitioner-Sri Sagar Maruti Bokade, has preferred MFA No.103437 of 2019 against the Judgment and Award dated 04th August, 2018 passed in MVC No.1948 of 2015, seeking enhancement of compensation.

8. The owner of the vehicle Smt.Rajashree has filed application under Order XLI Rule 27 read with Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure along with six documents seeking permission to produce the documents mentioned in the list as additional evidence.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:7834-DB 9.

Sri Vinay S. Koujalagi, learned counsel appearing for the appellant in MFA No.102573 of 2019 would submit that as per the complaint which is marked at Exhibits P17 and P17(a) in MVC No.1948 of 2015, the motorcycle involved is KA- 22/EP-4014.
This motorcycle is not of the ownership of the appellant and belongs to some other person.
The first respondent-claimant has intentionally lodged a false complaint against the appellant only to harass the owner of the motorcycle.

The Tribunal,
while adjudicating the Review Petition, has only considered the fact that the appellant did not lead any evidence despite having given an opportunity.

It is not correct to hold that when the appellant has not let in evidence, adverse inference could be drawn against that side and thus the impugned order is devoid of justifiable reasons and same is liable to be set aside.
He further submits that the fact that, case and counter case existed, was not disclosed by the first respondent as claimed in his claim petition.
However, the same was brought to the knowledge of the Court in the statement of objections filed by the appellant.
The Police filed false B report at a later stage and the same could not be produced.

The Tribunal has failed to consider the fact that the NC: 2024:KHC-D:7834-DB husband of the appellant-Mallappa Narayan Rajagolkar who was riding the Honda Activa tow-wheeler bearing Registration No.KA-22/EC-1563 had lodged a complaint before the Traffic South Police Station in Crime No.122 of 2015 and the said fact was suppressed.

There was an error Smt.Rajashree Mallappa Rajgolkar vs Sri.Sagar Maruti Bokade on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168445545/
4 apparent on the face of record and without considering all these facts, the Tribunal has erroneously held that the appellant herein is liable to pay compensation and has saddled liability on the appellant.

sentences.text:
Learned counsel further submits that the respondent No.1- claimant has lodged a false complaint before the Traffic South Police Station in Crime No.121 of 2015 alleging that on 10th July,
2015 at about 13.00 hours, that one Honda Activa vehicle two-wheeler Registration No.KA-22/EJ-4014, being ridden in a rash and negligent manner, came from the opposite side and rammed to the motorcycle of the respondent No.1-claimant.
Thus, this brings up a situation where there is a case and a counter case.
Further he submits that the investigation conducted by the Police is arbitrary and illegal.
The Police have filed a false B Report in Crime No.122 of 2015 whereas they have filed charge sheet in Crime No.121 of 2015 and in a situation where there is case and counter case
, filing of false B NC: 2024:KHC-D:7834-DB Report in one crime and charge sheet in another crime is arbitrary and illegal.
It is the submission of the learned counsel that the Police have not conducted proper investigation.

His further submission is that now the respondent has filed application under Order XLI Rule 27 read with Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure with the affidavit of Smt. Rajashree Mallappa Rajgolkar, wherein she has clearly stated as to the reasons for non-production of material documents shown in the list of documents and if the appellant/respondent No.1 is provided with an opportunity to produce the additional evidence, the same will be helpful to this Court to adjudicate the matter in dispute in accordance with law.

sentences.text: On all these grounds, he sought for allowing the appeal and to remand the matter to the Tribunal by providing an opportunity to the respondent No.1 to produce the additional evidence.
10. Sri Harish S. Maigur, learned counsel appearing for the claimant supports the Judgment and Award passed by the Tribunal.
He further submits that there are no grounds to interfere with the impugned Judgment and Award passed by the Tribunal and hence sought for dismissal of the appeal.
He further submits that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:7834-DB is on the lower side and hence, sought for enhancement of compensation.
Further, he submits that if this Court comes to conclusion to remand the matter to the Tribunal, then the Tribunal may be directed to dispose of the case within a period of three months.

11. Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties and having perused the entire appeal papers including original records, the following points would arise for our consideration:
1.

Whether the appellant in MFA No.102573 of 2019 has made out a cause for allowing the application filed under Order XLI Rule 27 read with Section 151 Code of Civil Procedure and remand the matter to the Tribunal?

sentences.text: We have examined the material placed before this Court.

It is the case of the claimant that on 10th July, 2015 at about 1.00 pm, one Omkar Mallappa Ajagolkar being the rider of motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-22/EJ-4014, rode the - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:7834-DB same from Ganeshpur-Belegavi Main Road to Hindalga-Belagavi Main Road, in a high speed, rash and negligent manner and while so riding near Vijayanagar Kannada Marathi School, dashed the said motorcycle against another oncoming motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-22/W-2009 and the impact of the accident is that, the claimant who was a pillion rider on the motorcycle bearing Registration No.KA-22/EJ- 4014, suffered grievous injuries.
Immediately, he was taken to BIMS Hospital, Belagavi for treatment and after receiving first aid therein, he was shifted to Vijaya Hospital, Belagavi for further treatment.
13. Respondent No.2-Insurance Company has specifically stated that the offending vehicle was not insured as on the date of accident.
Exhibit R1-copy of the insurance policy reveals that the motorcycle bearing Registration No.KA-22/EJ- 4014 was insured for the period 21st July 2015 to 20th July, 2016.
The accident occurred on 10th July, 2015.
There is no document to show that the vehicle in question was insured with respondent No.2-Insurance Company as on the date of accident.
Respondent No.1 is also charge-sheeted for the offence punishable under Section 196 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
On the basis of the evidence placed before it, the Tribunal Thad passed the judgment and award in question.

14. Respondent No.1 the appellant herein, has filed written statement contending that the petitioner-claimant was riding the motorcycle in a drunken condition with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and abruptly came on the right side of the road and dashed against the motorcycle of respondent No.1 and hence, the claim petition is liable to be dismissed.
Further, it is denied as to the other averments made in the claim petition as false.
Respondent No.1 has not adduced her evidence before the Tribunal.

During the pendency of the case before the Tribunal on 28th January, 2017, respondent No.1 had filed application under Order XVI Rules 6 read with Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure to issue summons to Vijay Ortho and Trauma Centre,
Belagavi to produce documents, discharge material, blood report, entire medical bills and prescriptions of Sagar Maruti Bokade, so also, documents pertaining to OPD No.R34291/15 and IPD No.9142 dated 10th July, 2015.

sentences.text: The Tribunal has allowed the said applications and summons were issued as sought for.
However, the respondent has failed to take steps.

Hence, on 21st June, 2017,
the Tribunal has passed that in spite of giving sufficient opportunity, the counsel is reluctant to take steps on IA.2 filed under Order XVI Rules 1 and 2 of Code of Civil Procedure.
Accordingly, the order passed on 12th April, 2017 on IA.2 was recalled and the case was posted for further cross of PW1.
Thereafter, cross of PW1 was recorded.

15. Now, along with the present appeal, the appellant- respondent No.1 before the Tribunal, has filed application in IA.I of 2021 under Order XLI Rule 27 read with Section 151 of Code of Civil Procedure to permit the appellant to produce documents mentioned in the list, as additional evidence.

This application is supported by the affidavit of Mallappa Rajagolkar, in which it is stated that the Tribunal has come to the conclusion that the owner, i.e. herself, is liable to pay the compensation.

The appellant has taken contention that the - 14 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:7834-DB motorcycle bearing Registration No.KA-22/EC-1563 is the one which involved in the accident and not the motorcycle bearing Registration No. KA-22/EJ-4014.

The accident occurred on 10th July, 2015 and the complaint was lodged by her on 11th July, 2015 mentioning that the vehicle involved in the accident was motorcycle bearing Registration No.KA-22/EC-1563.
First Information Report was registered based on the complaint.
The FIR was marked as Exhibit P17.
Based on the complaint of the husband of the appellant, summary No.111 of 2017 was registered and statement was recorded.
Summary No.111 of 2017 reveals that after investigation, the Investigating Officer has submitted the B report and same was accepted by the Court on 08th June, 2018.

Thereafter, the counsel for the complainant filed an application to advance the case and on 11th June, 2018 the Court passed the order permitting the complaint to file protest petition and contest the case.

Thereafter, on 30th November, 2020, the Court passed an order that there is a prima facie case to take cognizance for commission of offence under Sections 279 and 338 of Indian Penal Code and case was registered against Sagar Maruti Bakode, who was the rider of motorcycle bearing Registration - 15 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:7834-DB No.KA-22/W-2009 and accordingly, case was registered in CC No.461 of 2020.
Copy of the order sheet pertaining to CC No.461 of 2020 is also produced.

It is submitted that the vehicle involved in the accident was sent for motor vehicle accident report, and as per,
motorcycle bearing Registration No.KA-22/EC-1563 suffered damages, whereas the motorcycle bearing Registration No.KA-22/EJ-4014 has not suffered any damages.
The vehicle bearing No.KA-22/EC-1563, which was involved in the accident, was duly insured.
The additional documents proves that a false complaint was lodged against the appellant which can be made out from the motor vehicle report.
Therefore, the documents now sought to be produced are very much necessary to support her case and to do substantial justice to the parties and hence sought to allow the application.

Along with the application, the appellant has produced the following documents:

The copy of the policy pertaining to motorcycle bearing Registration No.KA- 22/EC-1563 is also produced, so also the wound certificate issued by Vijay Ortho and Trauma Centre, Belgavi pertaining to Sagar Mallappa Bakode and Omkar Mallappa Ajagolkar are also - 17 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:7834-DB produced.

However, the learned counsel for the claimant has orally opposed the applications and further submits that if this Court allows the applications and remand the matter to the Tribunal, then a direction may be given to the Tribunal to dispose of the case within three months.

Before filing this application under Order XLI Rule 27 of Code of Civil Procedure before this Court, the appellant has filed Civil Revision Petition No.8 of 2018 before the Tribunal under Section 114 read with Order XLVII Rule 1 read with Section 151 of Code of Civil Procedure to review the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal on the basis of the documents pertaining to Crime No.122 of 2015 and also the registration of Criminal case.

sentences.text:
It is well settled that Motor Vehicles Act, 1998 is a beneficial piece of legislation and as such, while dealing with compensation cases,
once the actual occurrence of the accident has been established, the Tribunal's role would be to award just and fair compensation.

As held by this Court in Sunita (Supra)
and Kusum Lata (Supra), strict rules of evidence as applicable in a criminal trial, are not applicable in motor accident compensation cases, i.e., to say, "the standard of proof to be borne in mind must be of preponderance of probability and not the strict standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt which is followed in criminal cases"."
17.

On careful examination of the material placed on record, we are of the view that the proposed documents are very much required to adjudicate the matter in dispute and also to do substantial justice between the parties.
Hence, it is just and proper to provide one more opportunity to the appellant/respondent No.1 before the Tribunal, to adduce additional evidence as sought for.
Accordingly, we answer point No.1 in the affirmative.

opennyai_summary.facts:
3. Relevant facts leading to filing of these appeals are that, the claimant preferred Claim Petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident.
On all the grounds sought for compensation.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
This motorcycle is not of the ownership of the appellant and belongs to some other person.
The first respondent-claimant has intentionally lodged a false complaint against the appellant only to harass the owner of the motorcycle.
The Tribunal,
while adjudicating the Review Petition, has only considered the fact that the appellant did not lead any evidence despite having given an opportunity.
It is not correct to hold that when the appellant has not let in evidence, adverse inference could be drawn against that side and thus the impugned order is devoid of justifiable reasons and same is liable to be set aside.
The Police filed false B report at a later stage and the same could not be produced.
The Police have filed a false B Report in Crime No.122 of 2015 whereas they have filed charge sheet in Crime No.121 of 2015 and in a situation where there is case and counter case
14. Respondent No.1 the appellant herein, has filed written statement contending that the petitioner-claimant was riding the motorcycle in a drunken condition with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and abruptly came on the right side of the road and dashed against the motorcycle of respondent No.1 and hence, the claim petition is liable to be dismissed.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the appellant in MFA No.102573 of 2019 has made out a cause for allowing the application filed under Order XLI Rule 27 read with Section 151 Code of Civil Procedure and remand the matter to the Tribunal?

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
13. Respondent No.2-Insurance Company has specifically stated that the offending vehicle was not insured as on the date of accident.
The accident occurred on 10th July, 2015.
On the basis of the evidence placed before it, the Tribunal Thad passed the judgment and award in question.
During the pendency of the case before the Tribunal on 28th January, 2017, respondent No.1 had filed application under Order XVI Rules 6 read with Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure to issue summons to Vijay Ortho and Trauma Centre,
Belagavi to produce documents, discharge material, blood report, entire medical bills and prescriptions of Sagar Maruti Bokade, so also, documents pertaining to OPD No.R34291/15 and IPD No.9142 dated 10th July, 2015.
The Tribunal has allowed the said applications and summons were issued as sought for.
Hence, on 21st June, 2017,
the Tribunal has passed that in spite of giving sufficient opportunity, the counsel is reluctant to take steps on IA.2 filed under Order XVI Rules 1 and 2 of Code of Civil Procedure.
Before filing this application under Order XLI Rule 27 of Code of Civil Procedure before this Court, the appellant has filed Civil Revision Petition No.8 of 2018 before the Tribunal under Section 114 read with Order XLVII Rule 1 read with Section 151 of Code of Civil Procedure to review the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal on the basis of the documents pertaining to Crime No.122 of 2015 and also the registration of Criminal case.
At this juncture, it is relevant to mention about the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of RAJWATI @ RAJJO AND OTHERS v. UNITED INDIA INSURANCE Smt.Rajashree Mallappa Rajgolkar vs Sri.Sagar Maruti Bokade on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168445545/
8 COMPANY LIMITED wherein at paragraph 19 of the judgment, it is held as under:

As held by this Court in Sunita (Supra)
and Kusum Lata (Supra), strict rules of evidence as applicable in a criminal trial, are not applicable in motor accident compensation cases, i.e., to say, "the standard of proof to be borne in mind must be of preponderance of probability and not the strict standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt which is followed in criminal cases"."
17.
On careful examination of the material placed on record, we are of the view that the proposed documents are very much required to adjudicate the matter in dispute and also to do substantial justice between the parties.
Hence, it is just and proper to provide one more opportunity to the appellant/respondent No.1 before the Tribunal, to adduce additional evidence as sought for.
